subject: Request: dataflow diagram + evidence for newly engaged third party
message_1_subject: Request: dataflow diagram + evidence for newly engaged third party
message_1_body:
Hi Claire,

Quick follow-up from our kickoff last week — we noticed in your subprocessor notice that FinVault recently onboarded a network/edge provider (DataTransit Inc.) that will touch logs and request metadata for API calls. To keep procurement and security moving on our side, could you please share the following:

- A one-page dataflow diagram showing exactly which FinVault services send data to DataTransit and which data classes are sent (PII, hashed identifiers, logs, request bodies).
- Confirmation of the legal basis and location(s) where DataTransit will process EU-origin data (country list).
- SOC 2 or ISO attestation for DataTransit (or an equivalent security questionnaire response).
- Details on encryption at-rest and in-transit; if KMS/HSM is used, please specify provider and whether keys are customer-controlled.
- Retention periods for logs and any ability to purge on request.

We maintain a layered DPA requirement for processors that handle request payloads; if you can include any redlineable DPA language or a pointer to your procurement contact, that would speed things up. I attached a brief template with the fields we usually need (I can forward a full DPA redline once we have the technical inventory).

Thanks — if easier, happy to jump on a 20-min call with your security or procurement folks this week.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

message_2_subject: Re: Request: dataflow diagram + evidence for newly engaged third party
message_2_body:
Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the note and the clear checklist. We did onboard DataTransit in July to help with edge routing and log aggregation for latency-sensitive endpoints. I attached a preliminary vendor inventory and our answers to the security checklist — these are initial responses while we pull together the formal diagram.

A few quick answers inline:
- Processing locations: EU (Ireland), US (us-central1), and India (asia-south1).
- Data categories to DataTransit: request metadata (headers, timestamps), routing metadata, and short-lived request traces. We do not send raw customer credit card numbers.
- Encryption: TLS in transit; AES-256 at rest with keys in our cloud KMS (AWS KMS). DataTransit has a dedicated customer keyspace but keys are managed by FinVault (not shared).
- Retention: logs kept for 90 days by default; we can configure shorter windows per-customer on request.

Attached: vendor-answers.xlsx, initial-inventory.csv. We'll produce a one-page dataflow PDF by end of day tomorrow and can share SOC 2 point-in-time report once legal signs an NDA (we can provide a link).

If you need specific DPA text, point us to your procurement contact and we can route the redline through them.

Cheers,
Claire Park
Security Operations Manager | FinVault
security@finvault.com

message_3_subject: Re: Request: dataflow diagram + evidence for newly engaged third party
message_3_body:
Claire —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups before we hand this to our legal/procurement team:

- Can you confirm whether DataTransit performs any content inspection (L7 payload parsing) or just transports metadata and traces?
- For AES-256 at rest with AWS KMS: are keys rotated on a customer schedule or by DataTransit? You said 'managed by FinVault' — can you confirm that means FinVault controls key rotation and access policies.
- Also confirm whether any processing nodes are in jurisdictions that would trigger export-control or data transfer obligations (we flagged India in our intake).

If easier, feel free to include a short sentence in the dataflow PDF that explicitly says "DataTransit does not store request bodies beyond ephemeral cache and does not perform content inspection" if that reflects reality. That will avoid a back-and-forth with our Legal.

I'll loop in Rishi from Legal to confirm what evidence we need for the DPA.

Thanks,
Jordan

message_4_subject: Re: Request: dataflow diagram + evidence for newly engaged third party
message_4_body:
Hi Claire —

Appreciate the details so far. Two procurement/legal asks before we can approve the processor in our DPA tracker: 

1) Please confirm in writing whether DataTransit performs any L7 payload inspection. If they do, provide a scope document describing fields parsed and retention limits. If they do not, a one-line confirmation is sufficient.

2) Please provide either (a) a SOC 2 Type II report for DataTransit or (b) a completed security questionnaire and an attestation from DataTransit that they are bound by your DPA with controls mapping.

3) Confirm key control: we need confirmation that FinVault controls the KMS keys used for DataTransit (no shared access by DataTransit personnel).

4) Export control flag: please confirm whether any processing or backups for DataTransit are stored in a jurisdiction that would require additional export control paperwork (we are especially concerned about non-EU, non-US storage).

For efficiency, you can upload evidence to the shared Drive link (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/finvault/dataflow-request-20260821) or sign and return the DPA redline (I attached our redline template). If you'd prefer, I'm happy to set a short call between our procurement and your procurement team — please share the best contact (we saw procurement@finvault.com on your domain).

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
